_comment: The stance dial, exhaustive. The generator this was born from (tests/go_fixtures.py) went with the interpreter in #272, so Go is the source of truth and this is maintained by hand -- carefully, and only alongside a decision that changed the dial. The tests re-derive every case from Status() and compare values AND key order, so an edit that does not match what the code emits fails rather than passing quietly. `describe` is recorded as a SERIALISED string rather than as an object because field order is part of the contract and only bytes carry it.

preset_blurbs.off: No calls, ever. The gate, the solver and the simulator all still work -- this turns off opinions, not the tool.
preset_blurbs.consultant: Speaks when spoken to, about what the gate already flagged.
preset_blurbs.second-opinion: Volunteers observations and looks at neighbouring cards. Still writes nothing.
preset_blurbs.collaborator: Questions the deck's axis and batches edits for one approval. Drafts a rationale only where you asked for one on an import, and marks every one it wrote.

modes.name: rationale-interview

modes.name: commander-dossier
modes.purpose: Who a deck's commander is, what archetype they define, and where they sit in Magic's history.

modes.name: research
modes.purpose: Answers a question about Magic from pages it read: the meta, a ruling in practice, a card spoiled ahead of the pool.

modes.name: theme-conversation
modes.purpose: Asks about you -- not about Magic -- until it knows enough to suggest a colour combination.

modes.name: theme-proposal
modes.purpose: Turns a theme conversation into two colour combinations and six pool-checked commanders.

modes.name: scan
modes.purpose: transcribe the text printed on a photographed card

modes.name: rationale-draft
modes.purpose: Drafts the `why` for cards that have none, marked as drafted, for a person to keep or rewrite.

modes.name: intake-filing
modes.purpose: Files an imported deck's cards under the macro categories the primer and the counts are built from.

axes.question: When may it speak?
axes.means: It may offer an observation when it has one.

axes.question: How far from the question may it range?
axes.means: The whole deck, including its axis.

axes.question: What may it change?
axes.means: It may assemble a batch for you to approve in one go.

payload.never: One rule holds at every setting: Claude never writes a card's rationale on its own. On an import you can ask it to draft the ones you have not written, and every sentence it drafts is marked as Claude's until you rewrite it.

modes.name: rationale-interview
modes.purpose: Asks about one card's slot so the user can write its rationale.

modes.name: slot-argument
modes.purpose: Makes the case against one card's slot. Never the case for it.

modes.name: commander-dossier
modes.purpose: Who a deck's commander is, what archetype they define, and where they sit in Magic's history.

modes.name: research
modes.purpose: Answers a question about Magic from pages it read: the meta, a ruling in practice, a card spoiled ahead of the pool.

modes.name: theme-conversation
modes.purpose: Asks about you -- not about Magic -- until it knows enough to suggest a colour combination.

modes.name: theme-proposal
modes.purpose: Turns a theme conversation into two colour combinations and six pool-checked commanders.

modes.name: scan
modes.purpose: transcribe the text printed on a photographed card

modes.name: rationale-draft
modes.purpose: Drafts the `why` for cards that have none, marked as drafted, for a person to keep or rewrite.

modes.name: intake-filing
modes.purpose: Files an imported deck's cards under the macro categories the primer and the counts are built from.
